publication_rule: This profile supports one metric. `claude_code.token.usage` is the only metric any fixture in this repository replays, so it is the only one named supported, and `gemini_cli.token.usage`, `gen_ai.client.token.usage` and `codex.turn.token_usage` are recorded as read surfaces with no capture rather than as planned or partial support. Nothing here is certification: `claude-code-otel-v1` is a candidate binding whose effective ceiling is private analytics, and a derivation table is a specification of a mechanism rather than evidence that any collector runs it.

supported_metrics.name: claude_code.token.usage
supported_metrics.note: Eight vectors: five datapoint series covering the four type values, cumulative-to-delta, a counter decrease, a start-time change and two concurrent query_source series, and three refusals covering an identity attribute, an unknown attribute and an unmapped category value.

unsupported_metrics.name: claude_code.cost.usage
unsupported_metrics.reason: A USD figure. Pricing is server-owned and a claim never carries a price, a currency or a cost estimate, so the receiver discards it before admission.

unsupported_metrics.name: claude_code.session.count
unsupported_metrics.reason: Counts sessions rather than tokens. Nothing in the accounting arithmetic consumes it.

unsupported_metrics.name: claude_code.active_time.total
unsupported_metrics.reason: A duration. Nothing in the accounting arithmetic consumes it.

unsupported_metrics.name: gemini_cli.token.usage
unsupported_metrics.reason: Read from a published configuration surface on 2026-08-06 and never exercised. No fixture in this repository replays a Gemini CLI export, so the type vocabulary, the instrument kind, the temporality and the reset behaviour are all unmeasured. Naming it supported would be a registry implying exercised support it does not have.

unsupported_metrics.name: gen_ai.client.token.usage
unsupported_metrics.reason: The OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic-convention metric the same CLI also emits. Emitting both means a naive receiver double counts, and no capture exists to decide which one the collector reads, so neither is consumed.

unsupported_metrics.name: codex.turn.token_usage
unsupported_metrics.reason: Read from a published configuration surface on 2026-08-06 and never exercised. Two execution surfaces are additionally silent under openai/codex#12913, so even an exercised capture of the interactive surface would not cover the producer.

capture_surface_hazards.default_state: Every datapoint of every Claude Code metric carries `organization.id`, `user.account_uuid`, `user.account_id`, `user.email` and `user.id`. This is the default and no capture has ever been observed without them.
capture_surface_hazards.receiver_obligation: All five are stripped inside the receiver, on the decoded in-memory datapoint, before admission to the observation queue and therefore before any aggregation, counter-delta state or grouping. A stripped value never keys a structure, never reaches disk, a log or a crash report, and a datapoint from which one cannot be removed is rejected whole. There is no partial-clean path and no identity here is ever trusted for identity: the ranked identity comes from the account and the device lineage, never from a telemetry attribute.
capture_surface_hazards.reference: D-099 fixes the strip list. OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_ACCOUNT_UUID=false removes the account UUIDs at the source and no documented setting removes user.email, which is why the removal is a receiver obligation and configuration is only a partial control.

capture_surface_hazards.default_state: Gemini CLI's `logPrompts` setting defaults to true, so prompt text is present on the telemetry logs channel unless the user explicitly disables it.
capture_surface_hazards.receiver_obligation: The collector never opens a logs channel for any producer. Ingesting it would import L0 content directly, and a receiver whose safety depended on a producer default being flipped would be relying on a setting it does not own. The metrics channel carries no prompt text and is the only admissible channel.
capture_surface_hazards.reference: docs/integrations/AGENT_INTEGRATION_RESEARCH_MATRIX.md, Gemini CLI row. The logs channel is unusable at any tier.

capture_surface_hazards.default_state: Codex CLI's `[otel]` configuration block defaults `metrics_exporter` to `statsig`, not to `none`. Enabling telemetry without setting the exporter explicitly sends token metrics to a third party rather than to a local collector.
capture_surface_hazards.receiver_obligation: No instruction, document or installer in this product may tell a participant to enable Codex telemetry without pinning `metrics_exporter` to an OTLP exporter aimed at the loopback receiver. The collector cannot detect or prevent the third-party export, so the control is the instruction and the control is weak; this is a reason the producer stays uncaptured rather than a hazard that capture would mitigate.
capture_surface_hazards.reference: Read from the published Codex CLI configuration surface on 2026-08-06 alongside openai/codex#12913. Recorded here and in docs/integrations/AGENT_INTEGRATION_RESEARCH_MATRIX.md; it was in neither before PF-041.

known_contradictions.other_value: cloud-separate-cache-v1 declares every one of its four source fields provider-reported
known_contradictions.effect: The same number is described twice with two different authorities, and provider-reported is the stronger evidence claim. The collector never sees a provider response: it sees a counter the CLI process emits, unsigned, and D-077 keeps every locally observed mechanism attested-local while D-100 records that no provider offers an individual-account attestation path. This profile writes runtime-reported, which is what docs/integrations/ADAPTER_ONE_CLAUDE_CODE_OTEL.md section 7 requires and what section 6 of the same document contradicts. Repairing it means registering a narrower accounting profile and re-pointing the binding, which changes the adapter's bound identity and is not this unit's to change.

derivations.rule: The literal 1, from the target schema's const.

A UUIDv7 the collector generates at normalization. OTLP carries no event identity, so two receivers of the same export mint two different values. The deterministic identity of the observation is local_fingerprint, not this.

Derived inside the adapter process from the session.id attribute through the keyed local commitment the binding's transform disposition requires. The raw identifier is discarded when the datapoint leaves that process, and the key is device-local, so the value is stable on one device and unreproducible off it.

Always null for this binding. query_source distinguishes main from subagent execution but names no parent, and the counter is aggregated per attribute set rather than per execution, so no linkage exists to read.
adapter_id claude-code-otel with the artifact and manifest digests of the running adapter build. Deterministic for a given build and not a property of the payload.

platform_profile_id comes from packages/schemas/platform-profile-registry-v1.json and capture_mode is otel. bundle_sha256 is the binding's certification tuple digest, which is null for every binding in this repository, and PF-016 made packages/schemas/normalized-event.schema.json admit that null rather than requiring a digest nobody has. Writing null is not a gap in this derivation: it is the derivation. The target schema pins an event whose bundle digest is null to a private-analytics disposition, so the field can now be written and cannot be written into a competitive claim.

claude-code, from the binding's certification tuple source_product_id. Not read from the payload: the instrumentation scope name is checked against the binding and a scope that does not match is not this producer.

Resolved from the registered model_id through the model registry. The OTLP payload carries a model alias and no provider attribute, so the provider is a property of the resolved model rather than of the export.

The model attribute resolved through the model registry to a registered identifier. An alias that does not resolve fails closed: the raw alias never advances and the event does not reach competitive eligibility.

The binding's accounting_profile id and content digest, which are cloud-separate-cache-v1 today. See the otel-count-authority contradiction: the profile that supplies this identity also declares an authority this capture cannot attest.

start_ns and end_ns bracket the export interval the delta covers, taken from start_time_unix_nano and time_unix_nano. generation is the reset counter the binding's value-decrease-or-start-time-change rule increments. domain_id is the collector's own clock domain and is device-scoped.

starts_at and ends_at from the datapoint's unix-nano times. uncertainty_ms is the configured export interval plus the measured receive-jitter bound, which is a property of the receiving machine rather than of the payload.

identity_source source-cursor-derived, and never source-assigned. A metrics counter names no execution: it is aggregated per attribute set, and query_source distinguishes main from subagent execution without naming either. What the source does produce is an ordered cursor - the attribute-set key with the counter start time and the export ordinal - so operation_ref is derived from source_cursor and the discriminator says so, which is the difference between deriving an identity and claiming to have read one. parent_operation_ref is null: the counter carries no linkage between a subagent execution and the one that started it. This is why packages/schemas/observer-equivalence-v1.json ranks this mode's achievable class at source-cursor and never at strong, and why two observers of one execution in different modes cannot be compared here.

collector_instance_id is the receiving collector's own device-local instance identifier and adapter_instance_id is the adapter process that decoded the export. Neither is in the payload and neither may enter the equivalence commitment preimage; they identify the channel so the exclusivity rule can tell two collectors apart, which is a different question from whether two observations are of one execution.

accumulation is the metric's declared temporality and reset_detection is the binding's declared reset rule, both read from conformance/accounting/producer-bindings-v1.json rather than from the export, because an OTLP payload states its temporality in the metric definition the binding pins. series_generation is the reset counter the value-decrease-or-start-time-change rule increments, which is the same counter monotonic_interval.generation carries. The claude_code.token.usage counter is cumulative, so every reading of it has to be differenced before it is an accounting input and packages/schemas/accounting-arithmetic-v1.json#reconciliation rejects one that has not been.

The counter delta per attribute-set key, placed by the binding's category_map: input to input_uncached, output to output_visible, cacheRead to cache_read, cacheCreation to cache_write. reasoning, multimodal_input and multimodal_output are structurally zero because the bound profile declares reasoning_semantics and modality_semantics unavailable. This is the one field the capture vectors replay, and it is the reason the map is called deterministic at all.

One entry per profile source field the datapoint carried, keyed by the binding's profile_source_field, each with containment exclusive because cloud-separate-cache-v1 declares no containment edge. A category the datapoint did not carry is an absent entry and never a zero.

runtime-reported. The counts originate provider-side and reach the collector through the CLI process carrying no signature, so the authority the collector can attest is the runtime that reported them.
none, from the bound profile's reconstruction.method. Nothing is tokenized locally on this path.

success, which asserts only that a counter increment evidences consumption that had already finalised when the CLI emitted it. The channel carries no outcome attribute, so this adapter can never emit failed-after-consumption or cancelled-after-consumption and cannot tell them from success. That is a capability limit of the mechanism.

scope none, ordinal 0, generation 0, distinct_execution false. The metrics channel exposes no retry fact and provider-side retries are already collapsed into one counter increment, so the duplicate domain rather than these fields is what prevents double counting. generation is zero for the same reason the other three are their neutral values: the channel says nothing about re-execution of a named operation, and it names no operation to re-execute.

domain_id claude-code-otel-datapoint, scope source-runtime. The key is the session commitment, the attribute-set key, the counter start time and the export ordinal, so a replayed datapoint is a duplicate rather than an addition.

A 43-character base64url keyed commitment over the duplicate-domain key. Keyed with a device-local key that is separate from any signing key, so it deduplicates on one device and reveals nothing off it.

bundle_id deterministic-rules-v1 with the disposition the local deterministic rules reached. It is a local outcome and never a ceiling: the binding's effective_ceiling is private-analytics and is applied by the server verifier, so an accept-local disposition does not make an event competitive.

policy_id claim-egress-v1 with result pass. A datapoint carrying any stripped attribute is rejected whole at the receiver and never becomes an event, so an event that exists has already passed; the field records which policy decided, not whether one ran.
null. No detector participates. D-053 keeps statistical and small-language-model detection local, advisory and post-launch, so nothing on this path produces a commitment.
false, a const in the target schema. A normalized accounting event never crosses the device boundary; only fixed-schema aggregate accounting and integrity claims do.
